chunks: And As-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, upon them be peace, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A woman is bequeathed to [as a ward], because Allah, the Exalted, says: "And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made a means of sustenance for you."'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating a type of dislike (karahah), because we have clarified previously the permissibility of bequeathing to women.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.يُوصَى إِلَيْهَا: bequeathed to / entrusted as a ward

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on entrusting a woman as a guardian over property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq links the legal concept of *tawliyah* (guardianship over property) to the Quranic prohibition of giving wealth to the *sufaha* (foolish or spendthrift), historically applied to women in certain contexts. Shaykh al-Tusi records Muhammad ibn al-Hasan’s clarification that this is not an absolute ban but indicates *karahah* (dislike/preference), thereby affirming the permissibility of bequeathing to women while cautioning against those prone to financial mismanagement.
